nodes.label: ESLint flat config (eslint.config.js)
nodes.rationale: Template config uses tseslint.configs.recommended; the doc recommends upgrading to recommendedTypeChecked / strictTypeChecked / stylisticTypeChecked for production so lint rules become type-aware, which requires parserOptions.project pointing at tsconfig.node.json and tsconfig.app.json.

nodes.label: React + TypeScript + Vite template stack
nodes.rationale: Minimal Vite setup chosen to get React working with HMR plus a small set of ESLint rules; Vite provides the dev server/HMR while `tsc` handles type checking.

nodes.label: @vitejs/plugin-react (Oxc-based)
nodes.rationale: Uses Oxc for JSX transform; alternative is @vitejs/plugin-react-swc which uses SWC instead.

nodes.label: @vitejs/plugin-react-swc
nodes.rationale: Alternative official plugin using SWC for faster transforms; chosen instead of the Oxc plugin when SWC tooling is preferred.

nodes.label: api (Bun backend service)
nodes.rationale: Root project is named 'api' and is scaffolded with `bun init`, positioning it as the backend half of the robotica-jlle system, separate from the Vite/React frontend.

nodes.label: index.html (Vite HTML entry shell)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately bare page: a single empty `<div id="root">` mount point plus one module script, so all markup is rendered by React and Vite owns bundling/HMR.

nodes.label: React Compiler (enabled)
nodes.rationale: Enabled on this template for automatic memoization, but documented as a trade-off: it 'will impact Vite dev & build performances'. The doc points at native Rust React Compiler support via `compiler: true` in plugin-react as a faster alternative to the Babel plugin.

nodes.label: Bun runtime toolchain
nodes.rationale: Bun is chosen as 'a fast all-in-one JavaScript runtime', bundling install, run, type check and format commands (bun install / bun run index.ts / bun check / bun fmt) into one tool, avoiding a separate node+npm+tsc+prettier stack.
